choices.why: A long off-white three-seat sofa on light birch legs is the cleanest Nordic anchor for the left wall and keeps the long room airy.
The olive-green wingback is a cozy, high-backed reading chair that brings the requested touch of green, and its light wood legs echo the other woods.
This pale ash coffee table with splayed legs is light and friendly, and its compact size leaves room to walk between the sofa and the armchair.
The plain warm-beige flatweave, 200x300, is big enough to sit under the whole seating group and adds a cream tone over the wood floor.
This light ash table is the largest candidate and seats six, with two chairs on each side and one at each end, in a fitting Scandinavian style.
These light beech chairs with paper-cord seats match the ash table and add warm natural texture.
The tiered bamboo pendant casts warm, patterned light over the table and fits the natural Nordic palette.
Its swing arm reaches over the armchair for reading, and the white drum shade stays calm and light.
The light natural elm and tapered legs bring warm wood near the dining area without darkening the room.
Semi-sheer sand linen softens the window wall and warms the white room while still letting the light through.
Two green linen-look cushions link the off-white sofa to the olive armchair and the plants.
A cream cable-knit throw adds cozy texture in the requested cream tones.
The tall, airy areca palm fills the corner between the two zones with fresh green.
A pair of these minimalist tree prints gives a quiet, Nordic graphic touch above the sofa; one alone would be too small for the wall.
A tall matte white stoneware vase holds green branches on the table or sideboard and suits the clean look.

answer.why: Light ash, beech and birch woods, cream and sand linens and knits, and green accents from the armchair, cushions and palm build a warm Nordic look that stays light along this long white room.
